label: GOD_NAMING_1: at each world the name designates the one existing being satisfying it there
definition: DescriptiveName o D is a partial name (TruthCore.Modal.RigidDesignation.Name) over the worlds of an Ontic model o. At each world v it designates x exactly when x alone, among the beings existing at v, satisfies the world-indexed description D at v (UniqueExistentAt: D v x, x exists at v, and every being that satisfies D and exists at v is x). The name is the description: at different worlds it may designate different bearers, or nothing. On the necessary-being node the description is a primitive parameter GodAt, where GodAt v x means that x satisfies at v a description that may vary by world; GodAt is deliberately not identified with sigma.IsGod. This is the attributive, Russell-style reading; a name whose sense is the description, evaluated at each world (narrow scope), has the same world-intension.
note: Analyst formulation, attribution deferred: not a sourced reading of Russell, Frege, Kripke or Aquinas. Uniqueness is actualist (candidates absent from v do not compete). GodAt is primitive: nothing relates it at other worlds to the world-invariant GOD_4 predicate sigma.IsGod; the open bridges NoOtherPossibleGod and GodhoodEssentialToGod state such relations. A source reading would need the semantics of divine names in a modal setting (for example ST I q.13) and is deferred.
